$comment: Central art-direction manifest. This is the ONLY place image selections live.
`node tools/build-art-images.mjs` reads this, normalizes tone/colour, generates
responsive WebP tiers into assets/images/art/, and writes _data/art.json with the
real pixel dimensions templates need. Templates never name a source file — they
call {% art 'slug' %}. To swap a photo, change `src` here and re-run the build.
roots:  reference = art-direction/sources/, the licensed stock pool. Prefer
these: they are the only photos shot by someone who levelled the
camera and nailed focus. Kept OUTSIDE assets/ deliberately — assets/
is passthrough-copied wholesale into _site, so a pool stored there
would deploy to production for no reason.
legacy = the 1.0 site's own image library. Its CORE pages only; the
per-sale galleries there are the bad phone photography. Caps out
around 2000px, so legacy sources suit cards, not full-bleed heroes.
sales  = 2.0/assets/images/estate-sales/<sale>/ gallery tiers. Same
bad photography — do not add new entries on this root.
fields:
slug      output basename + the id templates reference
root/src  where the source pixels come from
category  architecture | interior | object | detail | texture | people
rank      1 = hero-grade, 2 = large editorial, 3 = supporting/card
focal     object-position for crops ('50% 40%' etc)
ratio     art-directed output aspect ratio (w/h); omit to keep native
crop      optional pre-crop as ImageMagick geometry, applied before everything
tone      per-image overrides for the normalizer (see build-art-images.mjs)
alt       descriptive alt text
use       where it is placed (documentation only; templates are authoritative)

targets.$comment: Global tone targets. Every image is pulled toward these so the site reads as one body of work.

images.$comment: The egg sat at 47.2% of the frame while focal X was 55%, so CSS cover-cropping pushed it left of centre at every width. Measured in the 1440 render: the egg spanned x 590-745 of a 1600px-wide painted image with 88px clipped from the left, i.e. centre at 944/2000. Trimming the source to 1888 wide puts that centre at exactly 50%, so a symmetric focal keeps it centred at any viewport instead of only one.

images.$comment: Discovery cards stack heavy darkening on the photo — filter: brightness(0.94) plus a 0.50-to-0.72 black gradient (styles.css:783-789) — and then set a large serif title across the middle of it. That is a silhouette test, not an exposure one: an atmospheric interior tried here first read as mush even after being lifted to 0.47 mean luma, because it has no strong simple shape to survive the scrim. A white facade against sky does. Left brighter than the house target on purpose, so the card's own darkening lands it in the right place rather than below it.

images.$comment: Held down with saturation, not white balance. Raising wbStrength does nothing here: white balance anchors on the white patch (the brightest ~8% of the frame) and this frame's highlights are already neutral, so its gains came out 0.96/0.99/1.05 — well inside the clamp, nothing to unclamp. The cool cast lives in the midtones, out of that step's reach. Note the blue is mostly the building's own painted ironwork rather than a grade, so this is a restrained trim: pulled to 80% it sits closer to the warm house look, while a harder pull only turned real paint to mud.
